pr_title: fix: check each_blocks is empty on mount
pr_body:
fix: https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/8282

### Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following
- [x] It's really useful if your PR references an issue where it is discussed ahead of time. In many cases, features are absent for a reason. For large changes, please create an RFC: https://github.com/sveltejs/rfcs
- [x] Prefix your PR title with `[feat]`, `[fix]`, `[chore]`, or `[docs]`.
- [x] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves.
- [x] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.

### Tests
-  [x] Run the tests with `npm test` and lint the project with `npm run lint`

----------------------------------

## This pr fixes the bug

Bug can be seen in console https://svelte.dev/repl/1c3da5d4744c4820a1e9187f23fc6bbe?version=3.48.0
In my case, Firefox says `TypeError: can't access property "m", each_blocks[i] is null`

## What happens in code sample?

Several conditions and steps required:

* There must be UNKEYED each block with component binding
* Later on an array should be updated with lesser length, so holes would be produced
* Somehow remount children, e.g. wrap all with keyed each and update it
* This produces the code `each_blocks[i].m(...)`  without "is not null" check and it fails

## Some thoughts about the changes

* I've added 2 test cases, one with keyed each (passes on master) and similar without key (fails on master)
* I've added 2 same changes, both in keyed code generation and in unkeyed. This is for similarity, but maybe code size is more important here? If so, changes in keyed each can be reverted

issue_context.title: Nested #each throw errors when the inner and outer array change at the same time.
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

With a nested each loop where the inner loop is **not** keyed, altering the inner and outer arrays at the same time causes a runtime error.

## Conditions

Easiest to just check the REPL below, but the following conditions are required to reproduce this:

- Outer loop is keyed
- Inner loop is not keyed
- The array for the outer loop is altered so that one of its items moves to a different position.
- The array for the inner loop has one or more items removed.
- The inner loop contains a component (so that Svelte's outro handling code is added)
- The inner loop does not have any transitions

## Analysis

This seems to be a bug in how outros are handled. `each_blocks[i]` is set to null when the inner loop's contents go away, but if the inner components do not have a transition, this happens immediately, and so the mounting function then calls `each_blocks[i].m` before `each_blocks` has had its null values filtered away.

Off the top of my head, adding a null check inside the generated each_blocks mount loop should fix this, though I haven't tried it yet to verify. If we can use optional chaining in the generated code (don't remember what the target is nowadays) then this shouldn't involve much increase in generated code size. Maybe there's a more proper solution though.


## Workaround

Add a key to the inner loop, if possible

### Reproduction

REPL: https://svelte.dev/repl/b0f791216d2e466b824c671e27e1af79?version=3.55.1

Click the button that says "Break It" and see the error in the console.

### Logs

_No response_

### System Info

```shell
Svelte REPL
```


### Severity

annoyance
